## Problem

## Requirements

- Accept two string inputs, `s1` and `s2`.
- Assume that removing exactly one character from `s1` can yield `s2`.
- Produce all positions in `s1` where deleting the character leaves precisely `s2`.
- When identical characters allow more than one qualifying removal, report every such index.

## Preparation

- First write the exhaustive implementation as a reference for correctness, and afterward implement the O(n) scan that handles the duplicate run.
- Cover removals at the beginning, end, and interior, along with a repeated-character segment that produces multiple valid indices.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of comparing the two strings character by character to find the first point where they differ, which will guide you to the deletion position.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a two-pointer technique: iterate through both strings simultaneously, and when a mismatch occurs, skip the character in s1 and continue comparing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Consider the case where the differing character appears multiple times in s1, requiring you to check all possible deletion positions that yield s2.

</details>
